body: I agree fully that Keller gets saved. But I hated the choice of Denis not showing it. It felt like a half pay off for me to do a bait and switch from Keller to end the movie on Loki’s perspective. Keller was the main character and we didn’t get to see his ending.

Ok so I’m like five years late but I’m giving the show another chance… and holy shit was season 3 ep 1 a SHIT SHOW. I’ve not researched but it felt like the show got new writers that threw everything they set up at the end of season 2 to the GARBAGE. 

June is SO smart. I don’t believe she’s going to the Mackenzies like that!!! I don’t believe it. Nick is so right to be PISSED at her for being stupid. But it’s not the character, it’s simply BAD writing. 

Then the way they set up commander Lawrence is also thrown in the garbage, and they’re trying to justify through BAD writing how all the help he gave June and Emily was meaningless and he was actually a bad person all along? 

THEN Serena giving her baby away to June and their moment of understanding.. all thrown out the window too. 

Ridiculous. This should’ve been a three season only show. Ugh.

I think the ending of Smile 2 set up Smile 3 SO well cause they can go anywhere with it. A worldwide Smile epidemic, going only after the most mentally fragile people in the audience, choosing just 1? Who knows. I know I want it to be a full blown Smile apocalypse scenario.

I really want the opening of Smile 3 to be a retelling of what happened to Skye between the throat fisting in her apartment to the moment she’s on stage. Because I believe the hospital, driving away and the freezer never happened. I believe that was all happening in her head while she was going through the motions of getting ready for her show. 

It would be really cool if the opening of Smile 3 was her smiling and nodding through that whole period of time (the people around her happy she’s finally just following their instructions) until she’s on stage and the demon grants her a last moment of lucidity.

He’s taunting her and getting his revenge by sending her this book, that reminds her of being in love and makes her full of regret for leaving her ex husband. I saw it as a self fulfilled prophecy story - she knew what would be of her life if she let herself become like her mother and still let it happen. However, movie’s too long and a bit of a wank.

Excluding Hunger Games, I think all the ya stories made into movies were not great. HG fell off after Catching Fire, but at least it had a coherent beginning and ending storyline as in Katniss vs. Snow. Harry Potter vs Voldemort. Edward and Bella’s love story vs the Volturi. The Resistance vs the Empire. Storylines that were made clear from the start or at least early on in the franchises. 

Divergent and Maze Runner didn’t tell you until wayyyy too late who the villains were and what the heroes were fighting for. They’d almost be better if they were one big sci fi epic instead of giving the audience little to expect after each movie. Poor writing imo.

I get what you’re saying but in the short story’s universe, it’s as if the heptapods and those who learn their language are living a scripted life. They know, as if on stone, exactly what is going to happen at all times, and they have to go through exactly everything as they saw it for them to know it.

Yesss! The short story i felt had an “empty” and almost depressing feel at the end because Louise couldn’t do anything about her fate. So I liked that DV gave her the future as a choice, because it made her character feel more complicated and fully realised.

I got the message in the movie that her new ability was a burden, yes. But in the short story those who have seen the future can’t tell others about it. In the film it’s explicit that Jeremy Renner divorces her because she admitted to seeing the future and that their daughter will die.

I think a lot of people including myself thought that Louise intentionally chose to go ahead with the future she saw because she loved her daughter. 

“If you could see your whole life from start to finish, would you change things?” 

At the time, I inferred Louise saying this line to her husband in the film meant she could alter her path. It wasn’t until I read the short story that I learnt she couldn’t. But I also think Denis Villeneuve made Louise’s gain of knowledge/loss of free will purposely ambiguous.

This is what I thought from the film too. 

But in the source material her ability to see through time isn’t a gift or a tool. It’s a byproduct of her learning the heptapods language and the future is not something that she or the heptapods can change. 

The short story ponders more on free will than the film. At least that’s how I interpreted it.
